outcome: rehospitalization during the first month of life
cohort: The study included 208 infants with extreme leukocytosis (>40,000 cells/mL) and matched normal controls, with complete blood counts obtained on the first day of life.
finding: Extreme leukocytosis on the first day of life is a poor predictor of infection and was not predictive of a higher risk of morbidity in neonates.
